subject: Per-feature economics: follow-up & payback path
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wong <alex.wong@medvector.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Per-feature economics recap + next asks

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick written recap + concrete next asks so we can move the economics discussion forward with your CFO. Key points from our side: 

- Primary product areas under consideration: Smart Summaries, Contextual Search, and Clinical Triage assistant (these are the 3 features we scoped).
- Median tokens per call (your estimate): ~1.1–1.4k tokens for Summaries, ~700 for Search, ~1.6k for Triage.
- Volume signals you gave on the call: 30% DAU for the pilot cohort, target MAU ~200k over 6–9 months (first-year ramp).
- Ballpark total token volume (all features combined): 2M–9M tokens / month depending on adoption and sampling.
- MedVector target budget range for inference: $250–$450 per 1M tokens (you mentioned a range; flagged it as sensitive).
- Your commercial goals: 60% contribution margin target at the feature line; ~9 month CAC payback for pilot acquisition.

What Redwood will do next (action items):
1) Send a filled per-feature unit-econ template that maps tokens -> $/1M -> $/feature and shows CAC payback sensitivity (attached).
2) Provide two pricing bands (conservative & aggressive) that hit different margin targets given your stated volumes.
3) Run a quick sensitivity for the Triage assistant at 1M, 3M, and 6M total tokens to show $/feature and margin impact.

Please confirm the feature list above and whether we should include additional evaluation traffic (e.g., webhooks that will increase token counts). Once confirmed I’ll get the template populated and we can pencil in a follow-up call with Emma (CC) to walk the model.

Attachments: per_feature_econ_template.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Wong <alex.wong@medvector.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Hart <emma.hart@medvector.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-feature economics recap + next asks

Thanks Priya — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token estimates: the numbers you put for Summaries veer a bit high. Our telemetry shows median ~1,200 tokens for Summaries (peak 2–2.5k on long docs). Search is closer to 600–800. Triage can be 1.4–1.8k depending on dialog length; we can provide sample traces.
- MAU: the 200k is the upper-bound target for the full pilot group; initial launch cohort will be ~40k MAU for month 1, ramping to 200k by month 6.
- Budget: I mentioned $250–$450 but to be candid Emma (copied) will prefer starting conversation around $300/1M and see how that scales.
- CAC payback target: 9 months is correct; we need to see $/feature per MAU to model revenue share assumptions.

Can you include an example row for "Smart Summaries" showing: tokens per call, calls per MAU per month, resulting tokens per MAU, cost @ $300/1M and @ $400/1M, and resulting contribution margin assuming our average $/feature monetization of $3.50? That will make it easy for Emma to eyeball.

Also attaching two sample traces and a short usage snapshot.

Onwards — happy to jump on a quick 30m with you and Emma next week.

Best,
Alex Wong
Director, Product | MedVector Health
alex.wong@medvector.com
Attachments: medvector-usage-snapshot.pdf (pdf, 140KB); sample-traces.json (json, 48KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wong <alex.wong@medvector.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Emma Hart <emma.hart@medvector.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-feature economics recap + next asks

Alex / Emma —

Thanks for the samples, Alex. Attached is a first-pass per-feature model (redwood-per-feature-econ-v1.xlsx) and a short PDF that shows three sensitivity scenarios. High-level notes from the workbook: 

- Example assumptions used in the sheet (you can find them on tab "Assumptions"):
  • Smart Summaries: 1,200 tokens / call (median), 4 calls per MAU / month -> 4,800 tokens/MAU/month.
  • Contextual Search: 700 tokens / call, 2 calls per MAU / month -> 1,400 tokens/MAU/month.
  • Clinical Triage: 1,600 tokens / call, 0.6 calls per MAU / month -> 960 tokens/MAU/month.

- Cost math (illustrative): at $300 / 1M tokens, cost per MAU per month for Smart Summaries = 4,800 * $300 / 1,000,000 = $1.44. At $400 / 1M tokens that becomes $1.92.

- $/feature framing: if you price Smart Summaries as a $5/mo add-on and achieve 30% adoption among MAU, contribution margin looks like: 
  • Revenue per MAU (30% adoption): $1.50
  • Cost per MAU (at $300/1M): $1.44
  • Contribution margin per MAU: $0.06 (~4%), 
  • At $400/1M tokens contribution margin becomes negative (~-28%).

This highlights how sensitive margins are to token pricing and adoption. The attached sheet includes a CAC payback tab where we model customer acquisition cost per cohort and compute months-to-payback under different pricing bands; with a $120 CAC you get ~9 months payback at the $1.50 revenue per MAU scenario above (conservative adoption).

Next proposed steps: 
1) We can run the same per-feature rows using your cohort ramp (40k -> 200k) to produce a month-by-month P&L excerpt.
2) Ben can draft two pricing bands (volume-discount tiers) for procurement to consider: Band A (starter): $350/1M with modest commitment; Band B (commit): $275/1M with 12mo minimum and usage thresholds.
3) If Emma is open, schedule a 30–45m pricing walk-through next week to lock the band and procurement path.

Attachments: redwood-per-feature-econ-v1.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB); per-feature-sensitivity.pdf (pdf, 28KB)

Let me know what additional rows you want in the model (e.g., different monetization levels, different CAC assumptions). I’ll queue up the cohort ramp P&L once you confirm the initial cohort size and adoption assumptions.

Thanks,
Priya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Alex Wong <alex.wong@medvector.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Emma Hart <emma.hart@medvector.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-feature economics recap + next asks

Quick note from me — thanks for the model, Priya. Two tactical asks we should confirm on the next call:

1) Procurement cadence: will MedVector be able to commit to a 12-month minimum for Band B? If no, we should prepare a shorter-term band with a higher $/1M.
2) SLA/uptime/region requirements that materially change cost (if they require dedicated capacity or extra encryption we’ll model that as a separate line).

Priya — I’ll prepare the two draft bands and a short slide (1–2 pages) summarizing the margin impact at $275/$350/$425 per 1M. Alex — could you confirm whether Emma prefers a single consolidated deck for procurement or separate technical + commercial appendices?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
